# PERIMETERS The Incident Commander divides the colony into four areas. Changes are posted on the front page and can come at any time. If a sign and a Deputy disagree, follow the Deputy.
## OPEN AREA [color=#7FB2E5][bold]NO RESTRICTIONS[/bold][/color] - Living blocks, the mess, shops, the clinic waiting room and the bar. - No checks. Patrols pass through. Carry your ID anyway.
## CONTROLLED AREA [color=#E0B84C][bold]CHECKPOINT[/bold][/color] - Landing pads, fuel stores, the power plant, the atmosphere and water works, the comms relay and Colony Administration. - ID checked at entry. Bags may be searched. No loitering, no photographs.
## SECURED PERIMETER [color=#E06A5A][bold]AUTHORISED PERSONNEL ONLY[/bold][/color] - The command post, holding cells, evidence and weapons lockers, vehicle park and the perimeter fence line. - Entry only under escort with a written pass. Officers are authorised to use force to stop an intruder.
## INCIDENT PERIMETER [color=#F2F2F2][bold]DO NOT CROSS[/bold][/color] - Declared around a gas leak, a fire, a cave-in, a quarantine, unexploded charges, a hostage situation or an active shooter. - Nobody crosses the tape, residents or officers, unless assigned to the response. It is also a crime scene: touch nothing.
## MARKINGS - Chevron striping on a barrier marks the edge of an area. - Hazard striping marks a checkpoint lane. Stop at the painted bar. - Flashing lights and tape on a cordon mark an incident perimeter. Turn around.
Perimeter changes are also carried by the [netlink="Colony Herald" link="herald.colony.news"] when the press is on shift.
